executive_summary:
In the window from 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08, ARI3 collected 3,969 raw source records from 78 outlet domains. Final signal evidence was deduplicated so exact mirrors and syndicated or translated versions of the same publication count as one report evidence unit. The editor retained 22 signals. The largest by item count are sneaker (53 items from 16 outlets), denim (42 from 21) and vintage (28 from 17). Sneaker is concentrated, with 28 of its items from two outlets. Denim is the most widely spread, across 21 outlets, and includes coverage of two events: Demi Moore's denim gown at the CFDA Awards and the Met Gala 2027 theme. Vintage appears mostly in red-carpet and party dressing, including the CFDA Awards.

Suede (17 items from 10 outlets) and loafer (11 from 8) continue the autumn footwear and accessory coverage. Streetwear, leopard, minimalism, fringe, workwear, burgundy, maximalism and trench have 5 to 9 items each. The smallest clusters, with 3 or 4 items, are wide-leg, ballet flat, barrel leg, bomber, leather jacket, peplum, tailoring, kitten heel and oversized. These are patterns in the sources ARI3 collects, which were 89.1% editorial in this window. They do not measure consumer adoption or what people wear.

top_signals.name: sneaker
top_signals.evidence: Release coverage dominates: Nike Air Max and Air Jordan releases, including Space Jam Jordans also covered in an Italian-language GQ Italia headline (translated), NikeSKIMS, Lil Yachty's Air Force 1, New Balance releases with Kith and the Whitaker Group, ROSALÍA's ballet-themed New Balance campaign, Marni with Hoka, Denim Tears with adidas, Comme des Garçons' sneaker moccasin and Nike's sneaker boat shoe. Styling and trend items cover winter trainers, a German-language Vogue Germany piece on Vans (translated), adidas with leggings and Hailey Bieber's and Bella Hadid's sneakers. A sneaker museum exhibition and a sneaker-culture explainer add context, and two headlines present flats or other shoes as the alternative.
top_signals.index_note: The signal has 53 items from 16 outlets, editorial 50 and retail 3, on every day of the window. highsnobiety.com contributes 20 items and wwd.com 8, so 28 of the 53 come from two outlets. The editor labeled it stable.
top_signals.human_editor_note: Editorial view: ok, this is now marked as stable. Sneakers are forever.

limitations: Items are counted as style only when the ARI3 style classifier (frozen v0.0.2) gives a confident yes. On a 150-item prospective holdout of articles published after the classifier was frozen, its accuracy was 0.833, below its pre-registered 0.85 criterion (EXP-003A, H2 not supported). The editor reviews every evidence item used in this report.
In this window, 1,631 of 3,969 items (41.1%) received a not-sure prediction set and were excluded from style-positive counts.

In this window, 89.1% of collected items came from the editorial sector and 95.5% from the editorial group (editorial, trade intelligence and independent criticism). The stored corpus as a whole is 89.2% editorial sector.

The window has 0 items from social platforms, which are not collected, and 2 from resale sources. The report describes the language of the collected sources, not style culture, fashion consumers or the public at large.
Signal interpretation and evidence review are done by one editor.
ARI3 stores each item's headline and feed excerpt, not the full article.
0 of the window's 3969 items were stored before 2026-09-30, so their first-seen times are reconstructed from earlier records, not recorded as they happened.
Seven ambiguous lexicon terms (western, brat, demure, lace, bow, sustainable, glamour) are left out of every count until their uses are checked one by one.

Exact mirrors and syndicated, translated or lightly re-edited versions of the same publication across publisher domains are collapsed to one report evidence unit. The frozen source snapshot retains the raw records.
ai_assistance: ARI3’s deterministic pipeline surfaced candidate signals and bound the report to a frozen evidence snapshot. An AI assistant drafted the executive summary, evidence text, and index notes using only the locked report evidence, including translations of non-English headlines. The editor selected and merged signals, set labels and confidence overrides, pruned evidence, reviewed the drafted text, wrote the editor notes, and approved the final report.
